title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE REPATRIATION AND TREATMENT OF PRISONERS OF WAR OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA ARMED FORCES
title_original: 국군포로의 송환 및 대우 등에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE REPATRIATION AND TREATMENT OF PRISONERS OF WAR OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA ARMED FORCES

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Repatriation and Treatment of Prisoners of War of the Republic of Korea Armed Forces and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 1-2 (Scope of Remains)
The term "all or part of the body of a deceased Republic of Korea prisoner of war, as prescribed by Presidential Decree taking into account the feasibility of genetic testing and other factors" in subparagraph 1-2 of Article 2 of the Act on the Repatriation and Treatment of Prisoners of War of the Republic of Korea Armed Forces (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means any of the following:
1. The entire body of a deceased Republic of Korea prisoner of war;
2. Any of the following parts of the body of a deceased Republic of Korea prisoner of war that can be subjected to genetic testing:
(a) The head, chest, pelvic region, arms, or legs;
(b) Bones from the head, chest, pelvic region, arms, or legs.

Article 2 (Scope of POW Family Members from Places of Detention)
The scope of POW family members from places of detention under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Act shall comprise spouses (including de facto spouses) and children. However, POW family members from places of detention eligible for protection and support under Article 5(2) of the Act shall include the spouses of children and the grandchildren of Republic of Korea prisoners of war or returned prisoners of war who died during detention or before registration under Article 6 of the Act. <Amended on September 22, 2015>

Article 3 (Applications for and Decisions on Registration)
(1) A person who wishes to apply for registration as a returned prisoner of war or a POW family member from a place of detention (excluding family members of registered prisoners of war) pursuant to Article 6 of the Act shall submit an application for registration to the Minister of National Defense as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
(2) When an application for registration under paragraph (1) involves two or more POW family members from places of detention, they shall select a family representative. If they are unable to select a representative, the following order of priority shall apply:
1. Spouse;
2. Children (in order of age, beginning with the eldest, where there are two or more).
(3) The term "persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 4 of Article 6(2) of the Act means persons falling under any of the following:
1. Persons deemed to have no intention of returning to the Republic of Korea, including those whose return is feigned;
2. Persons who acquired foreign nationality after leaving their place of detention and have lived abroad for at least five years;
3. Other persons whose registration is deemed inappropriate in light of their conduct during detention and other relevant circumstances.
(4) The term "persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 4 of Article 6(4) of the Act means persons falling under any of the following:
1. Persons who have no materials proving that they are POW family members from places of detention of a deceased Republic of Korea prisoner of war;
2. Other persons whose registration is deemed inappropriate in light of their motives for entering the country, their conduct in the place of detention, and other relevant circumstances.
(5) Upon receipt of an application for registration under paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall decide whether to register the applicant and the applicant's grade within 30 days from the date of application if the applicant is a returned prisoner of war, or whether to register the applicant within 180 days from the date of application if the applicant is a POW family member from a place of detention, and shall notify the applicant of the result without delay. However, where unavoidable circumstances prevent a decision on registration or other relevant matters within the processing period, the period for making the decision may be extended by up to 30 days from the expiration of that period. In such cases, the Minister of National Defense shall notify the applicant in writing without delay of the extension and the reasons for it.
(6) The Minister of National Defense shall issue Returned Veteran Certificates and Returned Veteran Family Certificates to returned prisoners of war and POW family members from places of detention, respectively, whose registration has been approved under paragraph (5). <Newly Inserted on June 21, 2013>
(7) The Minister of National Defense shall prepare and maintain a registration ledger setting out necessary particulars, including the place of registration, family relationships, and career history of returned prisoners of war and POW family members from places of detention whose registration has been approved under paragraph (5). <Amended on June 21, 2013; December 23, 2025>

Article 4 (Detailed Criteria for Grade Determination)
The detailed criteria for determining the grades of prisoners of war registered under Article 6 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "registered prisoners of war") shall be as set out in attached Table 1.

Article 4-2 (Social Adaptation Education)
(1) The education provided to registered prisoners of war under Article 6-2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "social adaptation education") shall include the following:
1. Matters concerning the enhancement of an overall understanding of Korean society and culture;
2. Matters concerning the enhancement of an understanding of economic activities and basic legal knowledge;
3. Matters concerning the healing of physical and mental impairments sustained during captivity and in the course of escape from North Korea;
4. Other matters concerning the promotion of self-reliance and stable resettlement of registered prisoners of war.
(2) A registered prisoner of war who wishes to receive social adaptation education shall apply to the Minister of National Defense, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense, within 15 days from the date of receiving notice of the registration decision under Article 3(5).
(3) Where a registered prisoner of war applies for social adaptation education under paragraph (2), the Minister of National Defense shall commence social adaptation education within one month from the date of receiving the application.
(4) The period of social adaptation education shall not exceed six months.
(5) The Minister of National Defense may establish accommodation facilities, education and training facilities, and other facilities necessary for social adaptation education, or designate educational institutions equipped with such facilities as facilities for social adaptation education.
(6) Matters necessary for social adaptation education, including educational methods and curricula, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be determined by the Minister of National Defense.

Article 4-3 (Genetic Testing)
(1) The term "an institution prescribed by Presidential Decree that specializes in genetic testing" in Article 6-3(2) of the Act means the Ministry of National Defense Investigation Headquarters.
(2) Before conducting genetic testing, the Minister of National Defense shall obtain a written consent form from the person to be tested, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.

Article 5 (Calculation and Payment of Remuneration)
(1) The amount of remuneration under Article 9(1) of the Act (including allowances; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article) shall be calculated by applying the statutes and regulations on remuneration in force at the time the registered prisoner of war was detained: Provided, That where any remuneration has already been paid under statutes and regulations on remuneration, the amount so paid shall be deducted. <Amended on June 21, 2013>
(2) The following allowances shall not be included in the amount of remuneration under paragraph (1):
1. Overtime allowances, compensation for unused annual leave, holiday leave allowances, transportation subsidies, technical allowances, special location duty allowances, and special duty allowances for military personnel and others (excluding, among incentive allowances for military personnel and others, allowances paid to noncommissioned officers who have served as noncommissioned officers for more than 3 years);
2. Family allowances and subsidies for children’s educational expenses for the period during which the family of a registered prisoner of war received veterans’ benefits under the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State during that registered prisoner of war’s detention.
(3) Deleted. <June 21, 2013>
(4) The amounts corresponding to pay increments applicable to each rank until the retirement age for the relevant rank under Article 8(1)1 of the Military Personnel Management Act shall be added to the amount of remuneration under paragraph (1): Provided, That where a registered prisoner of war is a field-grade officer or above, longevity pay increments shall be calculated by applying Article 30-2(3) of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations.
(5) The amount of remuneration under paragraph (1) shall be calculated by converting it into the currency unit in use on the date of payment, without including interest.
(6) Remuneration under Article 9(1) of the Act shall be paid in a lump sum within 60 days from the date of registration. <Inserted on June 21, 2013>

Article 6 (Monthly Amount of Monthly Assistance Payable to Grade 3 Registered Prisoners of War)
The term “amount prescribed by Presidential Decree according to conduct during the period of detention” in Article 11(3)3 of the Act means the amount calculated by deducting from 6 times 43 percent of the standard median income the applicable amounts based on conduct during the period of detention as classified in the following subparagraphs. In such cases, the total amount deducted shall not exceed 50 percent of the amount equivalent to 6 times 43 percent of the standard median income. <Amended on January 19, 2016>
1. Where the person served as a member of the armed forces of detaining countries, etc., under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “detaining countries, etc.”): An amount corresponding to the proportion that the period of such service bears to the total period of detention;
2. Where the person caused harm to the Republic of Korea Armed Forces by providing detaining countries, etc., with information concerning the Republic of Korea Armed Forces or by other means: An amount equivalent to 40 percent of the monthly amount of monthly assistance;
3. Where the person participated in propaganda activities for the regimes of detaining countries, etc.: An amount equivalent to 30 percent of the monthly amount of monthly assistance;
4. Where the person engaged in improper acts while returning to the Republic of Korea, such as bringing persons falsely presented as family members: An amount equivalent to 30 percent of the monthly amount of monthly assistance;
5. Where the person joined public organizations or other such bodies in detaining countries, etc.: An amount equivalent to 20 percent of the monthly amount of monthly assistance.

Article 7 (Advance Payment of Lump-Sum Assistance)
(1) A person wishing to receive part of the lump-sum assistance before registration under the proviso to Article 11(4) of the Act shall apply to the Minister of National Defense for advance payment of lump-sum assistance, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
(2) A person other than a Republic of Korea prisoner of war who has left a place of detention shall, when applying for advance payment under paragraph (1), attach a power of attorney from the prisoner of war concerned and documents establishing the relationship with that prisoner of war: Provided, That where the Minister of National Defense deems that urgent circumstances prevent obtaining authorization from the Republic of Korea prisoner of war who has left the place of detention, the Minister may permit submission of the power of attorney after that prisoner of war has returned to the Republic of Korea.
(3) Persons who may apply for and receive advance payment of lump-sum assistance upon authorization by a Republic of Korea prisoner of war under paragraph (2), including cases in which a power of attorney is submitted afterward under the proviso to that paragraph, shall be limited to relatives of that prisoner of war (meaning relatives under Article 777 of the Civil Act): Provided, That where there are no relatives, a person recognized by the Minister of National Defense may do so.
(4) Where a person who received part of the lump-sum assistance under paragraph (1) obtained it by fraud or other improper means, the Minister of National Defense shall recover all or part of the lump-sum assistance received by that person.

Article 8 (Criteria for Recognition of Recipients of Survivor Assistance)
The criteria for recognizing a spouse or minor children who were supported by a registered prisoner of war at the time of that prisoner of war’s death under Article 11(5) of the Act shall be as set out in attached Table 2.

Article 9 (Payment of Survivor Assistance)
(1) A person wishing to receive survivor assistance under Article 11(5) of the Act shall apply to the Minister of National Defense for payment of survivor assistance, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
(2) Survivor assistance shall be paid in the following order of priority: <Amended on December 23, 2025>
1. The spouse;
2. Minor children. In such cases, where there are 2 or more children, the assistance shall be divided equally among them.
(3) Survivor assistance shall be paid in monthly amounts from the month following the month in which the registered prisoner of war died through the month in which the recipient loses the right to receive survivor assistance.
(4) Where a person entitled to survivor assistance has been missing for at least 1 year, survivor assistance for the period during which that person has been missing may, upon a claim by a person next in order of priority or a person of the same order of priority, be paid to that person. <Amended on December 23, 2025>
(5) A person entitled to survivor assistance shall lose that right upon falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. Where the person dies;
2. Where the person remarries, including entering into a de facto marital relationship;
3. Where the kinship relationship with the deceased registered prisoner of war terminates;
4. Where a person who has been receiving the assistance as a minor reaches 19 years of age.
(6) Where a recipient of survivor assistance in the last order of priority loses the right under paragraph (5), the person specified in the applicable subparagraph below shall report the grounds for loss of entitlement to survivor assistance to the Minister of National Defense within 30 days from the date on which those grounds arose:
1. Where the recipient of survivor assistance dies: The person obligated to report the death under Article 85 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations;
2. Where the recipient remarries or the kinship relationship terminates: The recipient;
3. Where a person who has been receiving survivor assistance as a minor reaches 19 years of age: The recipient.
(7) Where a person entitled to survivor assistance loses that right under paragraph (5), the right shall transfer to the person next in order of priority where such a person exists, and shall transfer to a person of the same order of priority where such a person exists. <Inserted on December 23, 2025>

Article 9-2 (Reduction of Consolation Assistance)
(1) Where a recipient of consolation assistance under Article 11(1) of the Act receives remuneration under Article 9 of the Act, a retirement pension, lump-sum retirement pension, or lump-sum retirement pension deduction payment under Article 21 of the Military Pension Act, or a retirement lump-sum payment under Article 28 of that Act, the amount received (in the case of a retirement pension, the amount converted into a lump-sum retirement pension under Article 21(3) of the Military Pension Act) shall be deducted from the lump-sum assistance under the main sentence of Article 11(4) of the Act: Provided, That where part of the lump-sum assistance was received before registration under the proviso to Article 11(4) of the Act, the amount shall be deducted from the lump-sum assistance remaining after the partial payment of the lump-sum assistance under the main sentence of Article 11(4) of the Act, and any deduction exceeding that remaining amount shall be deducted from the monthly amount of monthly assistance under Article 11(3) of the Act. <Amended on June 9, 2020>
(2) Any portion of the amount to be deducted under paragraph (1) that exceeds the amount of lump-sum assistance under the main sentence of Article 11(4) of the Act shall not be deducted.
(3) Amounts deducted from the monthly amount of monthly assistance under the proviso to paragraph (1) shall be deducted in installments over a period not exceeding 5 years: Provided, That where the person subject to the deduction dies, any amount remaining to be deducted shall be written off.

Article 9-3 (Reduction of Survivor Assistance)
Where a recipient of survivor assistance under Article 11(5) of the Act receives a survivors’ retirement pension under Article 30 of the Military Pension Act, a survivors’ disability pension under Article 34 of the Military Personnel Disaster Compensation Act, or a survivors’ pension for death in the line of duty under Article 35 of that Act, survivor assistance shall be paid after deducting from its monthly amount under Article 11(5) of the Act the amount received each month under Article 30 of the Military Pension Act or Article 34 or 35 of the Military Personnel Disaster Compensation Act. In such cases, any portion of the amount to be deducted each month that exceeds the monthly amount of survivor assistance shall not be deducted. <Amended on June 9, 2020>

Article 10 (Payment of Special Assistance)

(1) Special assistance under Article 12 (1) of the Act shall be paid within the limit of 250 million won according to the type of information provided or equipment (including goods) brought by a registered prisoner of war in the national interest, as follows:
1. Information of value for national security: Not more than 250 million won;
2. Warships, fighter-bombers, etc.: Not more than 150 million won;
3. Tanks, guided weapons, and other aircraft: Not more than 50 million won;
4. Weapons such as artillery, machine guns, and rifles: Not more than 10 million won;
5. Goods: An amount equivalent to their market value.
(2) The Minister of National Defense shall determine matters necessary for the specific amounts and methods of payment, etc. of special assistance under paragraph (1), comprehensively taking into account the actual value of the information provided and equipment brought by registered prisoners of war.

Article 11 (Housing Support)

(1) The Minister of National Defense may provide registered prisoners of war with support for security deposits and monthly rent pursuant to Article 13 (1) of the Act.
(2) A registered prisoner of war who intends to receive support for a security deposit and monthly rent pursuant to paragraph (1) shall apply for payment to the Minister of National Defense, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
(3) The Minister of National Defense shall determine the maximum amounts of support for security deposits and monthly rent under paragraph (1) for each grade under Article 6 (3) of the Act, taking into account rental conditions, such as rental security deposits and monthly rent, for rental housing supplied by the State, local governments, the Korea Land and Housing Corporation, or local public corporations under Article 49 of the Special Act on Public Housing; the maximum amounts of support for security deposits and monthly rent for Grade 3 registered prisoners of war shall be 80 percent of the maximum amounts of such support for Grade 2 registered prisoners of war. <Amended on December 28, 2015>
(4) A security deposit under paragraph (1) shall be paid only once within the maximum amount of support for security deposits under paragraph (3): Provided, That the difference between the maximum amount of support for security deposits under paragraph (3) and the security deposit for the dwelling first rented by a registered prisoner of war shall be paid in a lump sum upon that person's application after two years have elapsed from the date on which the registered prisoner of war filed a move-in report for resident registration.
(5) Monthly rent under paragraph (1) shall be paid in the amount specified in the lease agreement, within the maximum amount of support for monthly rent under paragraph (3), through the month in which the registered prisoner of war dies: Provided, That monthly rent shall not be paid for any period for which no lease agreement has been concluded.
(6) A registered prisoner of war who wishes to move into publicly constructed rental housing under Article 2, subparagraph 1-2 of the Special Act on Public Housing may apply to the Minister of National Defense for support for moving into publicly constructed rental housing, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense. <Amended on July 16, 2014; December 28, 2015>
(7) The Minister of National Defense who receives an application for support for publicly constructed rental housing pursuant to paragraph (6) may forward it to the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, the head of a local government, the president of the Korea Land and Housing Corporation, or other management entities for the relevant housing and request their cooperation; a management entity that receives a request for cooperation shall actively cooperate.

Article 12 Deleted. <December 3, 2014>

Article 12-2 (Grounds for Permission to Dispose of Rental Housing Provided as Housing Support)

The Minister of National Defense may, pursuant to Article 13 (2) of the Act, permit termination of a lease agreement for rental housing, assignment of a right of lease on a deposit basis or a leasehold right, or creation of a mortgage in any of the following cases:
1. Where a registered prisoner of war wishes to enter a medical care institution, welfare facility, etc.;
2. Where a registered prisoner of war has difficulty residing in the relevant rental housing due to a physical or mental disability or other unavoidable reasons.

Article 12-3 (Requests for Submission of Documents)

(1) Where necessary to verify facts relating to the payment of consolation assistance under Article 11 of the Act or housing support under Article 13 of the Act, the Minister of National Defense may require a person entitled to receive consolation assistance or housing support to submit relevant documents concerning changes in status, relocation, etc.
(2) Where necessary to verify facts relating to the payment of consolation assistance under Article 11 of the Act or housing support under Article 13 of the Act, the Minister of National Defense may request State agencies, local governments, or other public organizations to provide relevant materials. In such cases, an institution that receives a request shall comply with it unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 13 (Medical Support)

(1) A registered prisoner of war who intends to receive medical support pursuant to Article 14 of the Act shall submit an application to the Minister of National Defense, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
(2) The scope of medical support under Article 14 of the Act shall be as follows: Provided, That this shall not apply to a person who intentionally causes a disease, injury, or disability and seeks to receive medical support. <Amended on June 21, 2013; December 23, 2025>
1. Out-of-pocket costs of medical treatment received at a medical institution under the Medical Service Act (including medical treatment received for any of the reasons specified in the subparagraphs of Article 33 (1) of that Act);
2. Out-of-pocket costs of medicines dispensed according to a physician's prescription at a pharmacy registered under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act;
3. Out-of-pocket costs of purchasing assistive devices that supplement or correct functions of the human body (limited to cases where a medical institution under the Medical Service Act has confirmed that the purchase of such devices is necessary);
4. Out-of-pocket costs of caregiving (limited to cases where a medical institution under the Medical Service Act has confirmed that caregiving is necessary).
(3) The Minister of National Defense who receives an application under paragraph (1) shall decide whether to provide medical support and notify the applicant of the result without delay.
(4) The medical support payment determined pursuant to paragraph (3) shall be paid in a lump sum.

Article 14 (Assistance for POW Family Members from Places of Detention)

(1) Assistance under Article 15 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "assistance") shall be an amount determined by the Minister of National Defense, taking into account the inflation rate, etc., within the limit of 80 times the amount obtained by multiplying 200 hours by the preceding year's hourly minimum wage publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor under Article 10 (1) of the Minimum Wage Act as of the effective date of this Decree. <Amended on July 12, 2010>
(2) Assistance shall be paid to the family representative stated in the application for registration of POW family members from places of detention under Article 3; where no family representative has been selected, it shall be paid in the following order of priority:
1. The spouse;
2. Children (in order from oldest to youngest where there are two or more).
(3) An amount equivalent to one-fifth of the assistance shall be paid in a lump sum within three months after the decision to register POW family members from places of detention; the remaining amount shall be paid in four equal installments at half-yearly intervals after three months have elapsed from the date of the initial payment. <Amended on July 2, 2019>
(4) Where the family representative under paragraph (2) falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the person next in the order of priority shall become the family representative:
1. Where the family representative dies;
2. Where the family representative loses nationality;
3. Where the family representative falls under any ground for refusal of registration prescribed in Article 6 (4) of the Act;
4. Where the family representative has been missing continuously for at least one year;
5. Where the person specified in paragraph (2) 1 marries.

Article 14-2 (Assistance for Repatriation Expenses for the Remains of Republic of Korea Prisoners of War)

(1) POW family members who intend to receive support for expenses incurred in repatriating the remains of Republic of Korea prisoners of war pursuant to the first sentence of Article 15-2 (1) of the Act shall submit an application for payment of assistance for repatriation expenses to the Minister of National Defense, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
(2) Assistance for expenses incurred in the repatriation of remains under the first sentence of Article 15-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "assistance for repatriation expenses") shall cover transportation charges, daily allowances, lodging expenses, and meal expenses incurred in repatriating the remains of Republic of Korea prisoners of war. In such cases, the amounts of assistance for repatriation expenses for each item shall be as specified in Annex 2-2.
(3) Assistance for repatriation expenses shall be paid only once in respect of the remains of the same Republic of Korea prisoner of war and shall be subject to a limit of 15 million won.
(4) Where POW family members have selected a family representative, assistance for repatriation expenses shall be paid to that family representative; where they have been unable to select a family representative, it shall be paid in the following order of priority:
1. A person who bore the expenses of repatriating the remains of the Republic of Korea prisoner of war;
2. The eldest person.
(5) Within 30 days from the date of receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense shall determine eligibility for assistance for repatriation expenses for the remains of Republic of Korea prisoners of war and pay the assistance for repatriation expenses.

Article 15 (Employment Support for POW Family Members from Places of Detention)

The Minister of National Defense may, pursuant to Article 15-3 of the Act, provide POW family members from places of detention with assistance for career and vocational counseling, employment in military-related institutions such as military units, etc. <Amended on September 22, 2015>

Article 16 (Support for Use of Ancient Palaces and Other Facilities)

(1) The types of facilities that registered prisoners of war and POW family members from places of detention may use free of charge or at reduced fees pursuant to Article 15-4 (1) of the Act, and the rates of fee exemption or reduction, shall be as specified in Annex 3. <Amended on September 22, 2015>
(2) Registered prisoners of war and POW family members from places of detention who intend to use facilities under paragraph (1) free of charge or at reduced fees shall present the Returned Veteran Certificate or Returned Veteran Family Certificate under Article 3 (6) to the administrator of the relevant facility.

Article 16-2 (Honors for Republic of Korea Prisoners of War)

(1) The Minister of National Defense may accord honors pursuant to Article 15-5 (1) of the Act in accordance with the following categories:
1. Registered prisoners of war: Welcoming and retirement ceremonies;
2. Returned prisoners of war who died before being registered under Article 6 of the Act and Republic of Korea prisoners of war who died before returning: Interment ceremonies;
3. Invitations to various events hosted by the Ministry of National Defense, such as Armed Forces Day events;
4. Other matters that the Minister of National Defense deems necessary to honor Republic of Korea prisoners of war.
(2) A person who wishes to be accorded honors under paragraph (1) (meaning the bereaved family in the case of paragraph (1) 2) shall submit in advance to the Minister of National Defense an application for honors for Republic of Korea prisoners of war as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of National Defense.
(3) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (2), the Minister of National Defense shall determine whether to accord honors under paragraph (1), taking into account whether, during detention, the person sided with detaining countries, etc., engaged in hostile acts against the Republic of Korea, or engaged in conduct that set an example for military personnel, etc., and may vary the level of honors accorded.
(4) The welcoming and retirement ceremonies under paragraph (1) 1 shall be presided over by a general officer of the rank of major general or brigadier general, taking into account the registered prisoner's original unit of affiliation, etc.; where a registered prisoner of war engaged in conduct in keeping with the duties of a prisoner of war, such as serving a prison term for refusing to side with detaining countries, etc. during detention, the ceremonies shall be presided over by a general officer of the rank of lieutenant general or higher.

Article 17 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Personally Identifiable Information)

The Minister of National Defense (including the Ministry of National Defense Investigation Headquarters under Article 4-3 in respect of the duties specified in subparagraph 1) may process data containing genetic information under Article 18, subparagraph 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act (limited to the duties specified in subparagraph 1) and resident registration numbers under Article 19, subparagraph 1 of that Decree where doing so is unavoidable for the performance of the following duties:
1. Duties relating to genetic testing and the establishment and operation of a database of test results under Article 6-3 of the Act (including cases where that Article applies mutatis mutandis under Article 15-2 of the Act);
2. Duties relating to consolation assistance under Article 11 of the Act;
3. Duties relating to housing support under Article 13 of the Act;
4. Duties relating to assistance for repatriation expenses for the remains of Republic of Korea prisoners of war under Article 15-2 of the Act.
